claim: Each two-year Legislature begins at noon on the second Tuesday in January of each even-numbered year
quote: Each Legislature shall be constituted for a term of 2 years beginning at noon on the second Tuesday in January in each even numbered year

claim: Each legislative year begins on the second Tuesday in January
quote: The legislative year shall commence at noon on the second Tuesday in January of each year.

claim: Bills left at the end of the first annual session carry over into the second
quote: All business before either House or any of the committees thereof at the end of the first annual session may be resumed in the second annual session.

claim: The Governor has until noon of the 45th day after presentation to act on a bill
quote: shall be from the date of presentation until noon of the forty-fifth day next following

claim: A bill passed in the last 10 days of a two-year Legislature becomes law only if the Governor signs it by noon of the seventh day after the Legislature expires
quote: shall become law only if the Governor signs it prior to noon of the seventh day following such expiration

claim: The general election is the Tuesday after the first Monday in November every year
quote: The general election shall be held on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November in each year.

claim: The primary for the general election is the Tuesday after the first Monday in June, for all parties
quote: The primary election for the general election shall be held for all political parties upon the Tuesday next after the first Monday in June

claim: Every office filled at the November general election is nominated either by party primary or by direct petition
quote: shall be nominated directly by petition as hereinafter provided, or at the primary for the general election

claim: Voting in a party's primary makes the voter a member of that party until they file a change
quote: shall be deemed to be a member of that party until the voter signs and files

claim: A party member can vote in another party's primary only after switching at least 55 days before; new voters and voters who have never voted in a primary are exempt
quote: or a voter who has not previously voted in a primary election, may vote in a primary election of a political party unless the voter was deemed to be a member of that party on the 55th day next preceding such primary election

claim: A voter may declare themselves unaffiliated with any party
quote: or declare that the voter is unaffiliated with any party regardless of any previously declared party affiliation

claim: At the polls each primary voter names the party primary they want to vote in
quote: Each voter offering to vote shall announce his name and the party primary in which he wishes to vote.

claim: Whoever gets the most votes wins (plurality)
quote: for whom the greatest number of votes shall have been given therein for such office or offices, shall be deemed and taken to be elected

claim: Petitions for county and local offices on the November ballot go to the county clerk
quote: shall be addressed to the clerks of the respective counties wherein the officers nominated are to be voted for

claim: A petition candidate may carry a designation of up to three words that cannot use the name of a party that holds primaries
quote: The petition shall also state in not more than three words the designation of the party or principles which the candidates therein named represent

claim: Petition signers certify they have not signed another nominating petition, for the primary or the general election, for that office
quote: that they have not signed any other petition of nomination for the primary or for the general election for such office

claim: A petition may not nominate someone who has accepted a primary nomination for the same office
quote: No such petition shall undertake to nominate any candidate who has accepted the nomination for the primary for such position.

claim: A voter may sign one petition per office
quote: Such voter may sign one petition for each officer and no more

claim: A primary candidate for a municipal office cannot be another party's candidate for that office in the following November
quote: shall not be eligible to serve as the candidate of any other political party for that office in that municipality at the general election following that primary

claim: Borough: mayor elected at large for four years
quote: The mayor shall be elected by the voters of the municipality at large and serve for a term of four years

claim: Borough: six council members elected at large for three-year terms, two each year
quote: The council shall consist of six members, elected at large, and shall serve for a term of three years

claim: Borough elections are held every year at the November general election
quote: There shall be held annually, at the time provided by law for holding general elections, an election for borough officers.

claim: City: seven council members, six from two wards for staggered three-year terms and one at large for four years
quote: six shall be elected from two wards for staggered three year terms and one shall be elected at large for a four year term

claim: Cities that had a different mayor term or council structure before the 1987 law keep it until voters adopt the new one
quote: any city which elected its mayor for a two or three year term prior to the effective date of this act shall continue to elect its mayor for that term

claim: City elections are held every year at the November general election
quote: There shall be held annually, at the time provided by law for holding general elections an election for city officers.

claim: Town: mayor elected at large for four years and called the councilman-at-large
quote: The mayor shall be elected by the voters of the municipality at large and shall be known as the councilman-at-large.

claim: Town: eight council members, two from each of four wards, four-year terms
quote: The council shall consist of eight members, two elected from each of four wards.

claim: Town elections are held with the November general election
quote: The annual election for town officers shall be held at the same time and places as the general election.

claim: Township: a township committee of three or five members elected at large for three-year terms
quote: The township committee shall consist of three or five members elected at large and who shall hold office for a term of three years

claim: Township committee elections are held with the November general election
quote: The annual township election for members of the township committee shall be held at the same time and places as for the general election.

claim: A plurality elects a township officer
quote: A plurality of votes shall be sufficient to elect any township officer.

claim: The township committee chooses one of its members as chair, who is known as the mayor
quote: the committee shall have the power and authority to elect one of their number as chairman of the committee, who shall preside at all meetings of the township committee and who shall be known as the mayor of the township

claim: Village: a five-member board of trustees elected at large for three-year terms
quote: The village board of trustees shall consist of five members who shall be elected at large and serve for a term of three years.

claim: A village runs under the township law, reading township committee as board of trustees and mayor as president of the board
quote: shall operate and transact all of its business according to the laws pertaining to the township form of government

claim: The five kinds of municipality are city, borough, town, township and village
quote: means any city, borough, town, township or village.

claim: Nonpartisan municipal elections are held on the second Tuesday in May
quote: regular municipal elections shall be held in each municipality governed by this act on the second Tuesday in May

claim: The Secretary of State may move a May municipal election that falls on a religious observance
quote: the Secretary of State may change in any year the date provided for a regular municipal election

claim: The Uniform Nonpartisan Elections Law covers Faulkner Act charters, the commission form and other May-election forms, and governs only the time, manner and method of election
quote: This act shall govern these municipalities only with respect to the time, manner and method of election of municipal officers.

claim: The commission form is one of the forms that holds nonpartisan May elections
quote: commission form of government law

claim: Nonpartisan candidates may print a slogan of up to six words that cannot show party affiliation
quote: The designation shall not indicate political party affiliation.

claim: A May-election municipality may move its nonpartisan election to the November general election by ordinance
quote: may, by ordinance, choose to hold regular municipal elections on the day of the general election

claim: Once moved to November, a municipality cannot move back to May for at least 10 years
quote: at least 10 years have passed since the adoption of the ordinance changing the date of the municipal election to the day of the general election

claim: Nonpartisan municipal elections are decided by plurality by default
quote: the candidates receiving the greatest number of votes cast shall be elected to the respective offices

claim: A nonpartisan municipality can adopt or abandon runoff elections by referendum
quote: may, by referendum, adopt the provisions of those sections

claim: Where runoffs apply, the runoff is held on the fourth Tuesday after a May election, or in December after a November one
quote: shall be held on the fourth Tuesday next following that municipal election

claim: Nonpartisan municipal candidates file petitions with the municipal clerk
quote: the names of candidates for all elective offices shall be filed with the municipal clerk

claim: A voter may not sign more nonpartisan nominating petitions than there are seats to fill
quote: I further certify that I have not signed more petitions or certificates of nomination than there are places to be filled for the above office

claim: Municipalities that move their nonpartisan election to November stay under the nonpartisan elections law
quote: or having chosen to hold such elections on the day of the general election in November

claim: Faulkner Act municipalities hold May nonpartisan elections unless their charter puts elections at the November general election
quote: where the election of such officers is not provided to be at the general election

claim: Faulkner Act voters can amend the charter to switch between May municipal elections and November general elections
quote: the holding of general elections in November

claim: The Faulkner Act mayor-council plan
quote: mayor-council plan

claim: Mayor-council plan: mayor directly elected for four years
quote: The mayor shall be elected by the voters of the municipality, and shall serve for a term of 4 years.

claim: Mayor-council plan: council of five unless the charter says otherwise, four-year terms
quote: The council shall consist of five members, unless otherwise provided in the municipal charter, who shall serve for a term of 4 years.

claim: The Faulkner Act council-manager plan
quote: council-manager plan

claim: Council-manager plan: the charter decides whether the council or the voters choose the mayor
quote: That the mayor shall be elected by the members of the council

claim: The small municipality plan is open only to places under 12,000 people
quote: It may be adopted by any municipality having a population of less than 12,000 inhabitants

claim: Small municipality plan: council elected at large for three-year terms
quote: Members of the council shall be elected at large by the voters of the municipality and shall serve for a term of three years.

claim: The Faulkner Act mayor-council-administrator plan
quote: mayor-council-administrator plan

claim: A municipality changes its form of government by a majority vote of its voters
quote: vote in favor of adopting a change in their form of government pursuant to this act

claim: After adopting a Faulkner Act form, voters cannot vote on another form for 10 years
quote: may not vote on the question of adopting another form of government until 10 years thereafter

claim: The Faulkner Act is meant to give the greatest local self-government the Constitution allows
quote: is intended to confer the greatest power of local self-government consistent with the Constitution of this State

claim: Commission form: three commissioners under 12,000 people, five at 12,000 or more
quote: The commission shall consist of three members in municipalities having less than twelve thousand inhabitants

claim: Commission form: the commissioners choose one of their number to preside, called mayor
quote: the commissioners shall choose one of their number to preside at all meetings of the board

claim: Laws on counties and municipalities are construed liberally in their favor
quote: shall be liberally construed in their favor

claim: The Legislature may pass a special law for one municipality or county on its petition, which takes effect only if locally adopted
quote: the Legislature may pass private, special or local laws regulating the internal affairs of the municipality or county

claim: Cities are put in population classes for legislative purposes
quote: For legislative purposes, cities shall be classified as follows based upon population

claim: A city that moves to another population class is governed by that class's laws
quote: When any city becomes, by reason of its population, a member of another class

claim: Counties are put in population classes for legislative purposes
quote: For legislative purposes, counties are classified as follows based upon their population

claim: Every county is governed by an elected board of county commissioners
quote: the executive and legislative powers of the county shall be vested in that board of county commissioners

claim: Since P.L.2020, c.67, freeholders are called county commissioners
quote: shall be replaced by the term "board of county commissioners"

claim: County voters may set the board at three, five, seven or nine members
quote: increase or decrease the number of members of the board of chosen freeholders to three, five, seven or nine

claim: County commissioner terms are three years unless voters switch to four-year staggered terms
quote: to change the term of office for the members of the board of chosen freeholders from three to four years

claim: County clerks, surrogates and sheriffs are elected countywide at general elections; clerks and surrogates for five years, sheriffs for three
quote: County clerks, surrogates and sheriffs shall be elected by the people of their respective counties at general elections. The term of office of county clerks and surrogates shall be five years, and of sheriffs three years.

claim: County offices on the November ballot include county executive, sheriff, clerk, surrogate, register of deeds and the county board
quote: sheriff; county clerk; surrogate; register of deeds and mortgages

claim: Counties can adopt an optional charter by voter-approved charter study
quote: Shall a charter study commission be created to study the present governmental structure of

claim: One charter option is the county executive plan
quote: county executive plan

claim: A county executive is elected countywide for four years
quote: He shall be elected from the county at large for a term of 4 years

claim: Charter counties remain bound by general laws on elections
quote: the administration of the judicial system, education, elections, health

claim: Type II school districts hold their annual school election on the third Tuesday in April
quote: an annual school election shall be held in a Type II district on the third Tuesday in April

claim: Districts that moved their election to November vote with the general election
quote: An annual school election shall be held simultaneously with the general election on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November

claim: School election ballots carry no party designation
quote: No party designation shall appear on any ballot to be used in a school election.

claim: The school board or the municipal governing body can move the school election to November by resolution, without a vote
quote: may be moved to the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November without voter approval, upon the adoption of a resolution by the board of education

claim: A district can move back to April only after at least four November school elections
quote: No resolution may be adopted and no petition may be filed pursuant to this subsection until at least four annual school elections have been held in November.

claim: Elected school boards have nine members (or three, five or seven) serving three-year terms
quote: who shall be elected at annual school elections in the district for terms of three years

claim: School districts are classified as Type I or Type II
quote: School districts shall be classified as type I and type II school districts

claim: City school districts are Type I by default
quote: Every local school district hereafter established in a city

claim: Regional school districts are Type II
quote: Every regional school district

claim: In a Type I district the mayor appoints board members to five-year terms
quote: appoint one member of the board to serve for a term of 5 years

claim: A Type I district can switch to an elected board by referendum
quote: shall thereafter be elected by the voters of the district at annual school elections

claim: Fire districts elect annually, on the third Saturday in February or at the November general election
quote: An election shall be held annually either on the third Saturday in February or at the time of the general election

claim: A fire district that moves its election to November cannot move it back
quote: the date of the annual fire election shall be held at that time and shall not be changed

claim: A board of fire commissioners has five members
quote: to consist of five persons, residents therein

claim: Fire commissioners serve three-year terms
quote: of the third year following the year in which they were elected

claim: Fire commissioner candidates for a November election use the direct petition process
quote: shall be nominated by petition for direct nomination pursuant to the procedures set forth in R.S.19:13-1 et seq.

claim: Where runoffs are adopted, a candidate needs the most votes and a majority
quote: the candidates receiving the greatest number and a majority of votes cast shall be elected to the respective offices

claim: After a November nonpartisan election, the runoff is in December
quote: the run-off election shall be held at a special election on the subsequent Tuesday next after the first Monday in December

claim: Township voters can set the committee at three or five members
quote: The legal voters of any township may elect to increase or decrease the membership of the township committee of the township either to three or five members.

claim: The Commissioner of Education can move an April school election that falls on a religious observance
quote: the Commissioner of Education shall make any adjustments to the school budget and election calendar

claim: The annual school election can also carry a vote on extra school funding
quote: for the purpose of submitting a proposal to the voters for the approval of additional funds

claim: School board candidates may print a designation of up to three words that cannot use a party name
quote: the ballot for a school election may include a designation in not more than three words that conveys the principles which the candidate or candidates therein named represent

claim: Nonpartisan candidates for the same office can be grouped under one shared slogan
quote: If several candidates for the same office shall petition that their names be grouped together

claim: Faulkner Act voters can choose at-large or ward council elections
quote: the election of all council members at large

claim: Faulkner Act voters can choose staggered or concurrent terms
quote: the election of council members for staggered terms

claim: Faulkner Act voters can choose whether the council or the voters elect the mayor
quote: the election of the mayor directly by the voters of the municipality

claim: Faulkner Act voters can set council size at three, five, seven or nine
quote: a municipal council to consist of nine members

claim: Council-manager plan: elected council and appointed manager
quote: shall be governed by an elected council and by an appointed municipal manager

claim: Mayor-council-administrator plan: elected mayor and council and appointed administrator
quote: shall be governed by an elected mayor and council, and an appointed municipal administrator

claim: Mayor-council-administrator plan: mayor and council elected at the November general election
quote: The mayor and council shall be elected at the general election to be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

claim: Borough council terms are staggered so two seats are elected each year
quote: so that the terms of two councilmen shall expire at the end of each year

claim: City: mayor elected at large for four years
quote: The mayor shall be elected by the voters of the city at large and serve for a term of four years

claim: Town: mayor serves four years
quote: The mayor shall serve for a term of four years.

claim: Town: council members serve four years
quote: The members of council shall serve for a term of four years.

claim: Fire district candidates for a February election are nominated by petition
quote: candidates for membership on the board shall be nominated by verified petitions

claim: Naming a party on a voter registration form makes the voter a member of that party
quote: who indicates on a voter registration form the voter's choice of political party affiliation

claim: Party primaries are decided by plurality
quote: the person having in the aggregate the highest number of votes shall be the candidate of his respective party for the office to be filled
